facts.fact: Sea turtles have been around for over 100 million years — they outlived the dinosaurs.
Leatherback sea turtles can dive deeper than 3,000 feet.
A turtle's shell is made up of about 60 bones fused together, including its spine and ribcage.
Some turtles can breathe through their butts. Seriously. It's called cloacal respiration.
The temperature of the sand determines whether baby sea turtles are male or female.
Box turtles can live over 100 years in the wild.
Sea turtles cry — but it's just to flush salt from their eyes.
The largest turtle ever was Archelon, which was 15 feet long and lived 70 million years ago.
Turtles have excellent night vision due to an unusually high number of rod cells in their eyes.
Green sea turtles are named for the color of their fat, not their shells.
Some freshwater turtles can absorb oxygen through their skin while hibernating underwater.
A group of turtles is called a 'bale.'
Turtles don't have teeth. They use sharp beaks to tear food.
The spiny softshell turtle has a nose like a snorkel, letting it breathe while mostly submerged.
Loggerhead sea turtles migrate over 7,500 miles between feeding and nesting grounds.
Alligator snapping turtles lure fish by wiggling a worm-shaped appendage on their tongue.
Turtle shells have nerve endings — they can feel when you touch their shell.
The Galápagos tortoise can go a full year without eating or drinking.
Hawksbill sea turtles eat sponges that are toxic to most other animals.
Painted turtles survive winter by essentially freezing solid and thawing in spring.
The Mary River turtle grows algae on its head, earning it the nickname 'punk rock turtle.'
Tortoises helped inspire Charles Darwin's theory of evolution while visiting the Galápagos.
Some turtles can recognize their owners and will swim toward them.
Flatback sea turtles are found exclusively in Australian waters.
Mata mata turtles look like a pile of dead leaves — perfect camouflage for ambush hunting.
The oldest known tortoise, Jonathan, was born around 1832 and is still alive.
Baby turtles coordinate hatching by vibrating inside their eggs to communicate.
Sea turtles use Earth's magnetic field to navigate across entire oceans.
Turtle conservation efforts have brought several species back from the brink of extinction.
In many cultures, turtles symbolize wisdom, endurance, and the Earth itself.
